findings.title: Project premium-key fallback names no project
findings.problem:
For a premium model with no personal key, resolve_litellm_user_credentials returns the project's premium-models key (codemie:project:

:category:premium_models, is_personal=False). That skips the bypass at :945 and runs budget routing. When no project runtime is selected (admin non-member, no allocation in the category, dispatch None), :1001 now sets SPEND_ATTRIBUTION_PROJECT=None, but _apply_proxy_auth_header (:334-336) still authenticates with the project key and _create_global_budget_body_stream sets litellm_customer_id to the person. Before this change the header named the project on this path.
findings.impact: The project's LiteLLM key is charged but the spend row names no project, so the project ledger undercounts its key spend (AC4 partial). This also contradicts the new spend_logs_metadata.py contract that codemie_project names the project whose key was charged. Reachability confirmed: a live path from any premium-model proxy call made without a personal LiteLLM key.
findings.recommendation: Decide the intended attribution when a fallback call uses the project premium key. Option A: set request_info[SPEND_ATTRIBUTION_PROJECT] = project_name if user_credentials is not None and not user_credentials.is_personal else None on the fallback branch. That matches AC4 and the new contract, but the row then counts in both the project and personal figures because end_user is the person, which conflicts with AC2 and the :425 docstring. Option B: keep the project unnamed and stop authenticating personal-fallback calls with the project premium key. Add a parametrized test case for the chosen behaviour.
findings.check_notes: Mapped decision.outcome Option B with rationale; matches HITL code-review.final record in decisions.jsonl; command record head equals HEAD 93308c2.

fix.change: _apply_proxy_auth_header uses resolved user credentials only when is_personal; non-personal project premium key falls through to the app key on personal fallback

decision.outcome: Option B: send the caller's resolved credentials only when they are personal; a non-personal project premium key never authenticates a call, so a personal fallback goes out with the app key and codemie_project stays absent.
decision.rationale: Keeps AC2 (fallback spend counts in the personal budget only) and the codemie_project contract consistent: the key LiteLLM charges now always matches the project the row names, so no project key is charged without its ledger seeing the row.
